title: SF3000 Playbook
description: One vetted problem: how to detect it, what healthy looks like, how to fix it, and how to undo the fix.

description.description: One-line, plain-language statement of the problem.

symptoms.description: Free-text user complaints, used only for matching. Never executed.

command.description: READ-ONLY command. Must not mutate the system.

produces.description: How to turn the command's output into a measurement.

expect.description: The rule a healthy machine's measurement must satisfy.

risk.description: Governs whether the fix runs quietly, needs confirmation, or needs a snapshot first.

requires_privilege.description: Whether the FIX needs root/admin. Detect is read-only and must run unprivileged; the engine reads this flag only before a fix, and refuses rather than adding sudo itself.

reverse.description: How to undo the fix. The engine reads this to decide whether to snapshot before fixing and how to roll back after a failure.

strategy.description: command = an explicit undo command exists; snapshot_only = the only way back is a restore point (destructive/irreversible fixes); none = the fix is harmless or only touches regenerable state, so there is nothing to undo.

command.description: Undo command(s), keyed by distro or 'default'. Required when strategy is 'command'.

fix.description: Vetted fix command(s), keyed by distro or 'default'. Omit entirely for a detect-only (report, never fix) playbook.

verify.description: How to confirm the fix worked. Re-running detect is the default.

source.description: Provenance: who vetted this and where it was tested.
